Moving-target detection¶

Summary¶

MovingTargetDetection is the driver for the moving-target mode. It answers: as a ship moves along its route, when is it inside a valid reflection footprint, and what does the present signal model predict? It walks the ship trajectory, finds footprint-overlap candidates within a time tolerance, and – for each radio band – evaluates ocean, ship and thermal-noise terms. These are screening-level detectability metrics, not a full delay-Doppler detector or a calibrated probability of detection.

It ties the whole simulator together: it uses the propagated satellites, the reflection geometry (Specular reflection or Backscatter point / BRP), the ocean and ship RCS models, and the link budget. Its outputs (detection events, plots, an optional animation) are produced per band.

How a detection is scored¶

Geometry is solved once per transmitter/receiver pair, then the link budget runs once per band (each band has its own carrier frequency and transmit EIRP). The score depends on the mode:

  • Backscatter mode – the ship and the ocean are on the same path, so they can be compared directly. The signal-to-clutter ratio and the signal-to-clutter-plus-noise ratio are

    (70)¶\[\mathrm{SCR} = \frac{P_\mathrm{ship}}{P_\mathrm{ocean}}, \qquad \mathrm{SINR} = \frac{P_\mathrm{ship}}{P_\mathrm{ocean} + N_\mathrm{eff}}\]

    where \(N_\mathrm{eff} = N / G_p\) is a detection-equivalent noise scale: the raw thermal noise \(N = k\,T_\mathrm{sys}\,B\) divided by the coherent gain and the approximate incoherent sensitivity \(G_p = B\,T_\mathrm{coh}\,\sqrt{M}\), so \(N_\mathrm{eff} = k\,T_\mathrm{sys}/(T_\mathrm{coh}\sqrt{M})\) (see Link budget). The \(\sqrt{M}\) term represents reduced estimator variance; it is not a reduction of mean noise power. The gain is on the noise term only – the ship and the ocean carry the same GNSS code, so \(G_p\) cancels in the SCR and only lifts both above the thermal floor. A detection is declared when the SINR passes the configured threshold.

  • Specular (forward) mode – the ship is seen as a change in the forward glint: it blocks (shadows) the patch of sea it covers, so the detectable is the small drop in received power,

    (71)¶\[\Delta P_r = -\,P_\mathrm{ocean}(A_\mathrm{ship}),\]

    the ocean glint power over the ship’s waterline area (length x beam). It is reported on its own, as a fraction of the footprint glint, and against the noise floor. This signal is faint by design and is reported honestly, with no flooring.

Detailed Module Description¶

The detection loop¶

calculate_moving_target_reflection_intersection is the core. For each GNSS constellation it:

  1. takes the reflections that fall inside the trajectory bounding box and time window;

  2. for each one, checks whether the reflection point or antenna footprint overlaps the ship’s position within deltaT seconds of the matching trajectory time;

  3. on a match, evaluates the link budget per band – ocean power, ship power (if ship_dimensions is set), and noise – and records a detection event with its SCR/SINR (backscatter) or shadow change (specular).

An optimisation only propagates satellites inside windows with geometric satellite visibility (fn.compute_visible_times_and_resample_ship and fn.propagate_only_visible_satellites). Its default minimum elevation is the physical horizon (0 deg); the final antenna-frame steering and pattern gate is applied later.

Per-band evaluation¶

The reflection geometry does not depend on the band, so it is solved once per Tx/Rx pair. The link budget does depend on the band, so it is evaluated for each one in signals_per_constellation (carrier frequency, transmit EIRP, and code chip rate). Every output – events, plots, the SCR/SINR or shadow values – is therefore per band, and the band appears in the output filename. The entry script writes Footprint_overlap_<mode>_<CONST>_<band>_<contour>dB.png for the overlap maps and Link_budget_breakdown_<mode>_<CONST>_<band>_*.png for the power breakdown.

API reference¶

class object_definitions.MovingTargetDetection_def.MovingTargetDetection(sat_const, gnss_const, moving_target_object, antenna_obj, create_shapefile_for_visualization=False, deltaT=60, earth_model='spherical', reflection_mode='specular', link_budget_settings=None, bbox_buffer_deg=2.0, *, max_central_angle_deg, max_incidence_angle_deg, ship_dimensions=None, selected_signals=None)[source]¶

Find when GNSS-R reflections fall on a moving target and score detectability, per band.

Drives the moving-target mode. It walks the target trajectory, finds the reflections (specular or backscatter) that land on or near the target within a time tolerance, and – per band – evaluates the received power for the ocean, the ship, and the thermal noise to score detectability (SCR and SINR in backscatter mode, or a forward-shadow change in power in specular mode). Detection events and plots are produced per band.

Parameters:

  • sat_const (SatelliteConstellation) – LEO receiver constellation.

  • gnss_const (dict) – {name: SatelliteConstellation} of GNSS transmitter constellations.

  • moving_target_object (ShipTrajectory) – Moving target with a populated trajectory shapefile.

  • antenna_obj (RxAntenna) – Receiver antenna.

  • create_shapefile_for_visualization (bool, optional) – Also write a visualization shapefile (default False).

  • deltaT (int, optional) – Time tolerance [s] for matching a reflection to a target position (default 60).

  • earth_model ({"spherical", "elliptical"}, optional) – Surface model.

  • reflection_mode ({"specular", "backscatter"}, optional) – Forward mirror point or backscatter BRP.

  • link_budget_settings (dict or BistaticLinkBudgetSettings or None, optional) – Rx-system link-budget settings.

  • bbox_buffer_deg (float, optional) – Padding [deg] around the trajectory bounding box for plots (default 2.0).

  • max_central_angle_deg (float, keyword-only) – Maximum Tx-Rx central angle [deg].

  • max_incidence_angle_deg (float or None, keyword-only) – Maximum BRP incidence angle [deg]; required for backscatter, may be None for specular.

  • ship_dimensions (dict or None, keyword-only) – {length_m, beam_m, freeboard_m}; enables the ship-RCS contribution when set.

  • selected_signals (list of dict or None, keyword-only) – Validated [{band, constellation, freq_hz, eirp_dbw, chip_rate_hz}] plan from the INI bands.

Module Assumptions and Limitations¶

  • Two modes, two meanings. Backscatter gives a modelled ship-vs-ocean SCR/SINR. Specular gives only the forward-shadow change in power; it does not yet add the ship’s own forward glint.

  • Noise- or clutter-limited depends on settings. The SINR is formed against a detection-equivalent noise sensitivity scale: the detector divides thermal noise by \(B\,T_\mathrm{coh}\,\sqrt{M}\). The \(\sqrt{M}\) part is heuristic without an explicit detector statistic and false-alarm probability.

  • Footprint-resolution matching. A reflection counts as “on the ship” when the point or its footprint overlaps the ship position; the footprint is large, so this is a coarse spatial match.

  • No delay-Doppler coincidence check. The ocean return is evaluated at the reflection/BRP reference point and the ship at its own position. The code does not verify that both occupy the same delay and Doppler bin. Enabling the DDM-cell area therefore changes the assumed clutter area but does not make the candidate association a complete DDM detector.

  • No calibrated detection probability. detection_sinr_threshold_db is a user threshold on a deterministic metric. False-alarm probability, speckle, fading and measurement statistics are absent.

  • Ship return only when sized. Without ship_dimensions the run is ocean-only.

User Guide¶

This is the class behind python SRC/main_simulation_movingTarget.py (configured by Configuration_ship.ini). The relevant INI pieces:

  • [MOVING TARGET] – the ship route (see Ship trajectory).

  • [REFLECTION].reflection_type – "specular" or "backscatter".

  • [ANTENNA].bands – which bands (and so which constellations) to run.

  • [LINK BUDGET] – losses, the thermal-noise terms, and detection_sinr_threshold_db (see Link budget).

  • [OCEAN] – the sea state (see Ocean target).

  • [SHIP] – length_m / beam_m / freeboard_m to enable the ship return.

References¶

  • Ruf, C. et al., “A new paradigm in earth environmental monitoring with the CYGNSS small satellite constellation”, Scientific Reports 8, 2018.

  • Clarizia, M. P., Braca, P., Ruf, C. S. & Willett, P., “Target detection using GPS signals of opportunity”, Proc. 18th Int. Conf. on Information Fusion (FUSION), Washington, DC, 2015.
